[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.19 u/L
Jessica's BOCD has increased from before, but is still in the safe range. However, she has been out on the frontier for quite some time, and is often exposed to Originium products without proper protective measures, so we need to pay close attention to her.

'I'm actually more worried about her old injuries than about her getting infected.'
––Medical Operator from the Frontier Branch Office

lore.title: Archive File 1
lore.text:
We don't know precisely why Jessica set aside her mercenary career, and Blacksteel isn't particularly forthcoming about it. Whenever we bring it up, the person in charge always seems say something evasive before quickly changing the subject. However, it is true that Jessica has long been dissatisfied with Blacksteel's tough, uncompromising way of doing things, which the operators familiar with her had all noticed to some extent. On several occasions she has returned to Rhodes Island from a Blacksteel mission without outwardly displaying any negative emotions, but would instead lock herself in her room and not communicate with anyone for days at a time.
Afterwards, when we found out that she had been disciplined for disobeying her superiors, we realized that her differences with the PMC would be difficult to reconcile. This clash came to a head during a mission in the forested belt of Eastern Columbia, resulting in Jessica walking away from Blacksteel and her career, turning her back on both Fort Barron and the Brynley family to start over in a brand new land.
Fortunately, our partnership with her does not end simply because she severed ties with Blacksteel. The burdenbeast station she established on the frontier works together with our branch office to deliver medicine to remote areas that cannot otherwise be reached by vehicle, ensuring that sick pioneers can still get medication in a timely manner, while Jessica also needed funding to establish a frontier camp.
We are extremely pleased to be working together with her once again. While she may appear soft and shy on the surface, deep down she is actually tough and resilient. She also has a lot of empathy and is keenly aware of the emotions of others. These rare qualities allow her to comfort those who've suffered from various traumas, but also make her more susceptible to their emotions. It often takes her a long time to escape from that pain and sadness. Even more unfortunate is the fact that she stubbornly chooses to face everything alone. Despite everything she's witnessed and endured as a mercenary, Jessica has always been reluctant to share her experiences—not that it's our place to pry. But just by closely observing her behavior, we do believe that she's doing much better now.
At least, she now rarely isolates herself in the shooting range after returning to the landship from the frontier.

lore.title: Archive File 2
lore.text:
'Before officially participating in Blacksteel's field missions, Jessica had been working as a weapons tester in the Equipment and Applied Technology Department. There, she was exposed to a wide array of cutting-edge weaponry, and got to know many veterans retired from the Armed Personnel Dispatch Department. They were all experienced and could provide constructive advice during the weapons development process, and it's clear that Jessica has been heavily influenced by them, on top of her other experiences. Not only is she accustomed to using various weapons, but she's also proficient at modifying and improving them.'
'Uh huh.'
'In terms of weapon selection, Jessica prefers to carry a Blacksteel Model 1094 pneumatic handgun, a high-performance weapon representing the pinnacle of Blacksteel's sophisticated weapons R&D. As soon as it launched, it became the most popular gun of the year, beloved by mercenaries. But when faced with more complex situations, she will turn to a self-modified assault rifle, which is extremely accurate, powerful, and easy to assemble and disassemble quickly.'
'Uh huh.'
'Aside from those two commonly-used firearms, the presence of ships and armored vehicles in some extreme combat environments can pose serious difficulties. That's when she turns to a Raythean heavy-duty anti-armor/anti-ship cannon. And the accompanying tactical shield also takes mobility into account and can be used as a gun mount in addition to its basic protective function. Plus, the space inside the shield can be used to store additional small arms, ammunition, and other military equipment.'
'Uh huh.'
'But as you know, the battlefield is constantly shifting and requires thorough preparation each and every time, so Jessica tends to bring her entire arsenal with her, which greatly tests her load-bearing capabilities and arm strength. Now that she's out on the frontier, where the outdoor combat can be harsh and fierce bandits show up in convoys to rob supplies, she needs to carry not only her gear, but also extra supplies and—'
'Uh huh... So you're saying that's why you lost to her in 47 arm-wrestling contests in a row, even though you claim you can bench press 200 kilos. Gotcha.'
'......'
'Uh huh...?'
'Graaah––!'
––Excerpts from an everyday conversation between HR Operators

lore.title: Archive File 3
lore.text:
'Bernie Brynley and his wife already had a son and two daughters when they went on to have a third daughter in Jessica. As the family's youngest, everyone doted on her; not only were her parents extremely loving, but her brother and sisters were very close to her as well. There are reports that several of her promotions at Blacksteel were due to her family's support.
'While we don't know what sort of crime Jessica Brynley committed to get sent out to the frontier, it makes sense for a pampered rich girl who never learned right from wrong to be capable of just about anything. Yesterday, when confronted by doubtful reporters, Bernie Brynley still tried to defend his daughter, throwing his dignity to the wayside and screaming at them.'
'Bank robbery?! Where the hell did you hear that nonsense? Utterly ridiculous. Are you implying that there's a bank robber in MY family?'
'You'd best watch your mouth, sir. That's my daughter you're trying to slander!'
––Excerpts from the morning news of a Columbian TV station

'Their coverage of me was so one-sided.'
Turning off the TV, the girl looked back and addressed the operator behind her.
'Yeah, I agree. You're not like that at all, Jessica. Everyone here knows that.'
'No, that's not what I meant. They didn't even mention my grandfather, even though he was the one closest to me.'
'Huh? THAT'S what's bothering you?'
'Yeah. When he was with me, he didn't act like an elder at all, more like a playmate. When I was little, my favorite thing to do was sit in his arms and listen to him brag about his adventures out on the frontier, back when he was a soldier.
'Whenever he was done, he'd find his tie smeared with puree and cream. But that's just how it was. I was really little at the time. I was always eating, and would also crawl around all over the place... He really was the best grandfather ever.'
'What happened afterward?'
'Well... I grew up, and went off to secondary school in Victoria. Then he suddenly fell ill, and by the time I made it back home, he had already passed. I only had time to lay a bouquet of flowers in front of his tombstone.'
'I... I'm so sorry...'
'Don't apologize, I'm the one who brought it up. I'd never blame you for that.
'It's just nice having someone I can talk to about him...'
––Excerpts from a conversation between two operators while watching the morning news.

lore.title: Archive File 4
lore.text:
Everyone was shocked when they met Jessica out on the frontier. The girl in front of them was wearing coarse trousers and a plaid shirt, and behind her followed a neighing herd of burdenbeasts. She was riding barefoot on the lead beast, her skin flushed by the sun. If not for that familiar gun at her waist, nobody would've recognized that she was the same operator who used to work with us aboard the landship. After learning that we'd pass through the camp she was living in on our way to our destination, she offered to give us a ride. Quite fortunate for us, actually, since we were worried about damaging our vehicle at the time.
Atop the burdenbeasts, we headed up the river into a woodland. There, we discovered what life was like for her after leaving Blacksteel: in the middle of the night, several insects got through the tent's damage fabric. Be it the noisy buzzing of their wings or the itchy bumps from their bites, everyone was so fed up that they were swatting them one-by-one. But Jessica didn't seem to mind at all. She was simply curled up in a makeshift cot of two chairs pushed together, sleeping soundly. When an insect landed on her eyelid and left a huge bump behind, she simply rubbed it unconsciously before falling back into a deep slumber.
This one night was but a sliver of Jessica's hard-knock life. Not only did she need to deal with complex issues around the camp on a daily basis, she also had to deal with bandits and beasts periodically coming to harass her. Fortunately, she doesn't have to endure these things alone, as there are many people supporting her: the Elafia cook responsible for the camp's meals has exceptional skills, and even the most unpalatable ingredients are delicious in her hands; the old man tending the campfire has dexterous hands, and repaired our vehicle for us; there is also a girl there who is good with numbers, and is in charge of all the camp's finances; in addition, there's a Sankta hunter who's as good at herding livestock as he is ill-mannered, and he and Jessica take turns ensuring the security of the camp. Through everyone's mutual support, the newly-established camp quickly got on track and invited other pioneers to join.
Before we left, Jessica pointed to a forest in the distance and said this:
'We plan to buy a nice pine forest. On the frontier, logging is a relative secure industry, and good-quality white pine can be sold in a nomadic city for two hundred certs per cubic yard. That'll give us enough funds to build a small logging plate. Once we have a nomadic plate, everyone's lives will be that much better.'
As she spoke, her eyes let out a soft shine before becoming placid and calm again. During this whole exchange, her gaze remained fixed on that forest, not wavering for a moment.

lore.title: Promotion Record
lore.text:
'That's correct, Doctor. I participated in an armed robbery on the Davistown bank. That's just a fact, and I have nothing to dispute.'
The girl looks at you and rubs her hands together anxiously.
'However, I'm not on the frontier to serve out a sentence. I wasn't charged with any crime.
'Not because I was motivated by wanting to help the locals being extorted by the bank, but rather because... I'm not allowed to be guilty. Because Blacksteel operators cannot be guilty. Because members of the Brynley family cannot be guilty...'
The girl holds up a teapot in her hands and gives the tea leaves floating on the surface a blow, but accidentally cuts her lip on the container's broken rim.
'...You want to know if I plan to stay out here forever?
'Umm... I think I do. Because here, every choice I make belongs not to Jessica of Blacksteel, or to Jessica of the Brynley family.'
Wiping the streaks of blood from the corner of her lips with her fingers, the girl smiles shyly at you.
'They belong to me alone.'

lore.title: Profile
lore.text:
Patrizion is a citizen of Laterano entitled to the rights listed in Clauses 1 through 13 of the Laterano Constitution, and the longest-tenured active gun-knight of Laterano. He is intimately familiar with the use of various types of firearms.
In accordance with the memorandum of cooperation between the Lateran Curia and Rhodes Island, he is currently stationed on Rhodes Island as a collaborating operator under the code name Sankta Miksaparato.

lore.title: Clinical Analysis
lore.text:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Sankta Miksaparato shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.10u/L
Operator Sankta Miksaparato has many scars on his body, but all were properly treated, and in his fitness examination he demonstrated the physical prowess befitting a gun-knight, surpassing many younger field operators.
There is irreversible damage to his left hip joint. Surgical replacement is recommended, considering his age and the associated risk of bone fracture. I am available next month to perform the operation.
—Mon3tr

'I'm a little concerned. A gun-knight's presence on Rhodes Island represents Laterano's trust in us, but... Operator Mon3tr isn't nearly as meticulous as Dr. Kal'tsit was when it comes to dealing with people.'
'Don't worry, I just saw her pushing Mr. Patrizion's wheelchair through the corridor at great speed. He was laughing heartily.'

lore.title: Archive File 1
lore.text:
[A Day in Patrizion's Life]
05:00 - Wakes up and changes into full gun-knight armor. Typically takes one hour (he refused to pick a squire, insisting on wearing and removing his armor without assistance).
06:00 - Morning prayer. Typically takes one hour, though 10-15 minutes may be spent deciding which scripture ribbon to display on his armor (scriptures issued during Yvangelista XI's reign are excluded from selection).
07:00 - Arrives for duty. Patrizion leads his squad to patrol the designated district, wearing a halo amplifier (a.k.a. helmet-mounted supplemental halo light). Laterano guidebooks recommend that tourists in need of assistance seek out the brightest halo in the crowd.
13:00 - Change of shift. Patrizion climbs the walls and uses city-defense artillery loaded with special ammunition to clear obstacles in Laterano's route. Laterano is the only nomadic city that maintains its route by such means, and only the gun-knights are skilled enough to destroy large obstacles (typically overgrown Originium crystals) without compromising the terrain of the route. This is his favorite part of the day.
17:00 - Change of shift. Patrizion arrives at the firing range for practice or to train new Pontifica Cohors recruits, and demonstrates the usage of large firearms to the numerous Lateran citizens who gather to watch. Typically takes much longer than expected due to the large crowds, but he never turns down citizens seeking his advice.
19:00 - Audience with Yvangelista XI to report on Laterano's security matters, discuss the Law, and share cactus tarts (as the previous item on the schedule tends to overrun, Patrizion typically only has time to do the latter).
20:00 - End of work day. Patrizion blocks Yvangelista XI's work account, removes his personal account from the blacklist, picks out a message that includes movie tickets from the many unread messages to reply to, then turns off his terminal.
20:30 - Watches a movie with Yvangelista XI.
22:00 - Attempts to sleep (usually unsuccessful, in which case he turns on his terminal and attempts to send a message to Yvangelista XI's personal account, only to get a popup message that he has been blocked).

[Audio Log]
'Why don't you answer his messages? Weren't you the only one to realize that he disappeared when we were dragged into the dream by the Law? I thought you guys were good friends.'
'Mm... all I remembered was that there was this old man who gave me the habit of eating cactus tarts, but I couldn't remember who it was. Speaking of, you're friends with Mostima, aren't you, Fia? Why don't you answer HER messages?'
'......'

lore.title: Archive File 2
lore.text:
It took six months before Operator Fiammetta and Operator Sankta Miksaparato met on Rhodes Island. She promptly looked up his mission logs and found that the gun-knight, despite claiming to want to find a place outside Laterano to get some good rest, had participated in a large number of field missions, along with other even more outlandish activities:
At Roberta's introduction, he starred in the Wrankwood action blockbuster Kingdom of Outlaws. He had showed up at just the right time—the filmmakers were having trouble casting someone more than two meters tall who could play a villain, wear a special suit of armor, and carry a massive weapon that sprayed fire. Conveniently, he was able to do all this without special effects or even a custom costume: all the crew had to do was spray-paint his gun-knight armor. He was extremely interested in acting, and turned out to be a natural, finishing most of his scenes in one take. The producer called him 'the last piece of the puzzle for this film to become a classic'...
He also took part in a Columbian off-road rally—it took the combined efforts of Closure and Chiave's team and a full month of work to create a vehicle that could carry his weight and that of his armor, but the final result was unsatisfactory at best: though no one was foolish enough to clash with him, the machine lacked the necessary performance, and the massive rider and his massive bike were the last to cross the finish line at sunset. Though the photo album 'Gun-knights and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance' became the subject of much discussion on the intercity net.
......
Items such as 'helping Engineering with deck repairs' and 'learning qinggong from Yanese operators' were dismissed by Fiammetta as being mundane.

'Is this your idea of rest and recuperation, Patrizion? You're even busier than you were in Laterano.'
'Did you think I'd spend my days on the deck basking in the sun?'
'......'
'Sure, that sounds like what an old man on the verge of retirement might do. But I've spent my entire life as a gun-knight and nothing else. What's wrong with a chance to experience other ways of living?'
'I didn't even say anything!'
'Look, Fia, I won't interfere with your life anymore, so I hope you won't interfere with mine either... There might not be much left of it, but there are still so many possibilities.'

lore.title: Archive File 3
lore.text:
It is difficult to define the relationship between Patrizion and Fiammetta.
They are not your average grandfather and granddaughter. He took her in when she was seven, vowing to his fallen comrade to raise her into a Lateran any parent would be proud of. Their first 'war' broke out that very day, when he attempted to comfort the young Liberi with movies when she stubbornly refused to show her sorrow. The attempt was a failure, with Patrizion being forced to defend his choice of films (though he insists it was a win because he achieved his original goal of making her forget her sorrow). The adoption documents at the Notarial Hall record their relationship as grandparent and grandchild, but they rarely call each other that. Indeed, during what little time they spend together, they are like two bickering friends, arguing over each other's fighting styles, interests, hobbies, behavior, and even diet, before going back to their own lives, satisfied.
They are also not your average mentor and pupil. Patrizion was indeed Fiammetta's mentor, and he was involved in the important moments of her life, from choice of school to choice of career. According to her, however, he only seriously exercised his role as a mentor on three occasions: accompanying her when she upgraded her grenade launcher, encouraging her to join the gun-knights, and attempting to rectify her tastes in cinema. He did not deny these claims, and simply reiterated his disapproval of her prejudice against Wrankwood movies.

[Medical Department Audio Log]
'Ah, it's nothing I can't talk about... I've always felt that my role as her mentor was to be the embodiment of Laterano for Fia. As a Liberi child who lost her parents at a young age, she had many questions growing up that 'Paradise' had to answer, questions that couldn't be answered by the papers of the Notarial Hall, or the 'faith' that every Lateran speaks of yet can't properly explain. For Fia, I was a gun-knight, someone who was in a position to interpret the Law. I was a Lateran she could talk to... Honestly, I was in the same boat. After Gia left the Holy City and Pag distanced himself from me—when I realized I'd never truly shared anything with the Liberi I lived side-by-side with—I began to have doubts about the Holy City, and needed a 'Laterano' I could talk to. That was when Fia came into my life. Who's to say who couldn't leave whose side?'
'I see. But why don't you want her to find out that you'll be hospitalized for a while because of arthritis?'
'Because I don't want her to think of me as a bedridden old man.'

lore.title: Archive File 4
lore.text:
[Postcard]
Dear Grandmother,
I will graduate soon. I would like to apologize for the impulsive decision I made behind your back... Perhaps you already realized that I've felt out-of-place studying theology these past four years. I still believe that my childhood dream is my destined path, and that I can do so much more as a gun-knight than as a priest.
I'll be applying to become a cadet gun-knight, so I won't be coming back for the holidays. The training and approval process may take a while, but I'll be in full armor the next time I come see you.
With Love, Patrizion
[Notice Letter]
Mr. Patrizion Pozzo,
We regret to inform you that we have held the remains of your grandmother, Marion Pozzo, for the maximum period permitted. As we have been unable to contact you, we have cremated her remains in accordance with the Law. You may retrieve the ashes at your convenience.
With Apologies, Ecclesia Requietum Stevonus

[Permit]
Patrizion Pozzo, Apostolic Knight, is hereby authorized to supervise the departure of the long-range landship Twinflower and accompanying vehicles from Laterano, for the purpose of deporting Lateran citizens afflicted with Oripathy in accordance with the Law.
Patrizion Pozzo is hereby granted absolute discretion over all personnel on the ship, and is authorized to make any modifications or cancellations to the schedule as necessary.
[Notification]
Citizen Gia Lopez, you have been diagnosed with Oripathy, and are now scheduled to depart Laterano on the landship Twinflower in accordance with the Law.
Cooperate with supervising personnel during the journey, and remain in the Infected cabins on the lower levels except when necessary. Detailed instructions are attached with this notification. Please read them prior to departure.

[Recommendation]
Your Holiness:
I, Patrizion Pozzo, hereby recommend the cadet gun-knight Aurela, who demonstrated extraordinary performance during the assessment process. While her pride can still get in her way at times, I believe that with proper guidance she could be the most promising gun-knight of the next generation.
Patrizion Pozzo
[Rejection]
To Patrizion Pozzo, Apostolic Knight:
As the Pontiff of Laterano, I hereby reject your resignation. What happened to Aurela was not your fault—not entirely, at least—and there is still much for you to do in your current position.
If you still insist on resigning and nothing will change your mind, write another resignation letter.
Yvangelista XI

[Unsent Letter]
...Gia.
I retired today. I've been a gun-knight for fifty years... It's plenty, but at the end of it all, I still don't understand what a gun-knight is.
At first, I thought becoming one would let me protect everyone.
Later, I thought becoming one is what made me lose everyone around me.
Recently, however, an even scarier thought occupies my mind. Maybe all the ups and downs in my life had nothing to do with becoming a gun-knight at all.
That it's not that being in this position made all those choices for me, but that I was unwilling to make them myself... Was becoming a gun-knight the only choice I ever made in my life?
If so, a 'gun-knight' might be no more than a symbol, an ideal, an answer for me that I'd taken for granted.
But that's not what a gun-knight should be, and it's not what Laterano should be. No one should allow a symbol, an ideal, to dictate all their choices in life. Do you think I still have a chance to help the children understand this?
Or maybe they've always understood it better than I have.
I hope so, Gia. I really do...

lore.title: Promotion Record
lore.text:
It has been a long day. You were unable to get out of work until quite late, and the movie has already started by the time you arrive at the theater. You feel less guilty when you sit down and see that the seat next to you is empty; it would be rude to be half an hour late for a meeting with an old man, but not so much if the other party is late too.
The movie ends, and the old man never showed up. As you get ready to return to your office, someone pats you on the shoulder.
'You were late, Doctor.'
You turn around to see the tall figure of Patrizion, his head wrapped tight in a scarf that almost covers the top of his head. It has been a cold winter.
You express your dissatisfaction. After all, it was he who never showed up. He sighs and apologizes.
'The people behind me complained I was too tall, so I moved to the last row. Sorry, I forgot to send you a message.'
Now you are the one in the wrong. You blink.
'I usually pick the late shows, where I won't have to worry about blocking someone else's view. For some reason, though, I always have someone sitting behind me, so I always have to go sit in the last row. At my age, it gets really hard to see the screen from there...'
Patrizion keeps talking along the way, right up until you have to part. That is when he realizes it—
'Oh, look at me, I've been babbling, haven't I? It's been so long since I've watched a movie with someone, and I was just too excited.' He shakes his head abashedly and turns around to leave.
You stop him before he rounds the corner and tell him you were planning to get some ice cream. You can walk with him for a little while longer.

lore.title: Archive File 1
lore.text:
Soon after Yu arrived at Rhodes Island, Nian went into the kitchen and gave the perfectly functional facilities a complete makeover before dragging her little brother in.
Later that day, as Nian was digging into a spicy hotpot, she was joined by the typically reclusive Dusk, and Yu prepared several small dishes for her. Shu, Chongyue, and Ling soon joined the party, and all the family members on Rhodes Island came together to enjoy a fine meal at the same table—a sight that made the Yanese operators tasked with monitoring them quite nervous.
When they were done, some of them disappeared immediately, while the rest cleaned up, did the dishes, and apologized to the logistics operator on duty, drawing this little event to a close. The logistics operator swallowed his complaints at the sight of the bags of rice Yu offered him, and the bowl of rice balls in sweet wine soup on the table.
He did not realize that doing so even once would make it that much harder to refuse Yu in the future.
The next day, Yu showed up in the kitchen again as though he were meant to be there, showing off his Yanese cooking.
By day three, he started walking around while cooking, observing how others cooked.
By day four, he started arguing with people over whether a dish needed more scallions or more salt.
By day five, he could be seen engaging the other cooks in shouting matches that were only a little less heated than his cooking wok.
In just a few days, he had blended in with the rest of the kitchen. Although the food served at the cafeteria was not affected, none involved will forget the chaos in the kitchen at the time. However, the operator who was supposed to be in charge seemed to have little interest in reigning things in, largely because of the osmanthus cake he was munching on.
'Mm... jushleddembee... mm,' he said.
After a rather hectic adjustment period, the 'Young Chef' has become a constant presence in the kitchen. In addition to Yanese cuisine, he is also making forays into other areas, trying his hand at baking bread, searing steaks, and rolling sushi, which he said was important for satisfying the palates of Rhodes Island's diverse population.
'Is that why you stole the pizza and custard tarts?'
'Hey, how am I supposed to make them if I haven't tried them before?'

lore.title: Archive File 2
lore.text:
A package from Baizao lay before Yu. At first, he took it into the kitchen thinking it was the ingredients he had procured from Yan, only to hurry back to his room with it after opening it up.
At the top of the package was a letter from Jiang, the only employee of Savors at Yu's, and the restaurant's acting chef and manager in Yu's absence. The usual complaints: how hard it is running a tiny operation, how tight the budget is, and imploring Yu to return. He made a mental note to tell Jiang to be more creative about his pleas the next time he is back in Baizao.
At the end of the letter, however, Jiang mentioned something else: An old ledger hidden in a space in the walls, which the workers discovered while they were renovating the kitchen. Jiang made a copy and sent the original to Yu, per usual practice.
Yu silently praised Jiang for being on top of things, and put the letter aside to look at the ledger, which was pitch-black from years of being smoked. He had tucked it away because it was practically being marinated, only to forget about it when he left.
Being a tiny operation, it was also Yu's job to keep track of transactions, something that became a habit over time. He wiped the soot off the cover and flipped it open.
It was a record of daily income and expenses. There was a mark next to outstanding accounts, which are checked off as they are paid.
Most of the time, the outstanding accounts were for tiny sums—patrons who had forgotten their wallets. The next time they came back, be it hours or days later, they would either place the money they owed on the table, or discreetly pass it to the waiter along with the bill for the current meal, along with a little gesture to keep it quiet.
A few pages later were the banquets held over the course of a year, from weddings to funerals, to celebrations for promotions or winning competitions, ranging anywhere from a few tables to a few dozen. These are expensive affairs, and Yu's typical practice is to ask only for necessary expenses to be paid up front; the rest can be paid in due course, as the customer's circumstances permit. In cases of hardship, Yu has even footed the up-front bill, allowing the banquet to go ahead first, and the debt paid later. Many customers choose to pay their debts in kind, be it in the form of ingredients, kitchen utensils, furnishing, or advertising. If he really dug into things, he might very well find that he is the one who owes a favor now.
Yu flipped through a few more pages.
So many people come and go. Some debts are settled, some are not. Ji had criticized his lackadaisical attitude towards bad debts, when profits were slim to begin with. 'This was why the restaurant remains so tiny and unknown, despite being around for so long,' he said.
Well, Yu was a chef, not a businessman. He flipped through the ledger, checked off a few old accounts based on the note that Jiang had sent along as well, and put it down next to a notebook with the Rhodes Island logo on the cover.
The connections between people were not measured in numbers, after all.

lore.title: Archive File 3
lore.text:
For most families, it would be perfectly normal for siblings to run into each other and sit down for dinner. Yu would love to have this kind of normalcy, but could hardly help it, being what he is.
Therefore, he does his best whenever his siblings come to Baizao for whatever reason, whether they are taking up a new position, making a report to the Sui Regulator, or simply passing through.
Shu's tastes are light and simple. She always brings plenty of rice, sometimes even insisting on cooking for her little brother herself. White rice with steamed meat and vegetables—a simple meal that brings out the natural flavor of the ingredients.
Ji is always about efficiency. If he is just passing by, he would be content with a simple and inexpensive meal. If he wants to sit down for a full course, though, one would be in for a long day, forced to listen to him review each and every dish, one by one. On the other hand, when he does, there will be no need to worry about rent for the month—it is Ji who owns the building, after all.
Nian is the biggest eater of the bunch, and the place is liveliest when she is there. One could smell her favorite hotpot from a hundred meters away, and she likes to invite the other patrons to join her, even Sui Regulator agents. Yu encourages those who cannot handle spicy food to decline the offer—he has seen such patrons carried out on stretchers after sampling Nian's hotpot.
Dusk is always picky, right down to the timing of the meal. Take too long, and she is no longer in the mood when it is served. Fortunately, Yu knows a trick: a particular combination of fine appetizers, fruits, and desserts that even the mercurial Dusk is always in the mood for, though this will not stop her from complaining.
Ling's visits are usually about booze. A warm pot of wine, a plate of appetizers, let her drink to her heart's delight, and she's gone before you know it.
One would imagine Chongyue preferring the stockbeast meat of the north, given that he has spent most of his life guarding the borders, but he always asks Yu to serve him something he has never tasted before. From north to south, from east to west, all that flies, all that walks, all that swims, and all that grows from the ground—Yu must constantly try out new ingredients and new cooking methods just to satisfy his oldest brother. It was for Chongyue that Yu made his first pizza and Siracusan dumplings.
The one who tends to the gardens outside Baizao likes his dishes matched in complementary manner. Occasionally, he will bring delicacies from afar and ask Yu to find a match. The results may be a pleasant surprise even to Yu himself.
The musician is easy to tend to: she asks for the menu and orders from it like anybody else, sparing Yu from needing to think about it. Once she has finished the meal, however, she always takes out her instrument and starts singing, turning the restaurant into an impromptu opera house, with more patrons listening than eating.
...As for Wang, all Yu remembers is that he had the same tastes as the sister who was once at the academy. Neither were picky: serve the normal four dishes plus soup, and they were perfectly content. But Yu's memory grows fuzzy... Yu was always happy eating with her. She was never picky, and always complimentary, every comment highlighting Yu's thoughts as he was cooking the dish. But Wang... He always ate in silence.
Whenever the siblings leave, a few plain-clothes patrons would write something down in their notebooks, then pay the bill and follow them out the door. They are undoubtedly here on official business, but they are also paying customers, and he never confronts them. It is just like their family, whose powers keep the officials of the imperial court up at night. But here at the restaurant, sitting at the table, they are no different from any other family getting together for a meal.
Late at night, when the restaurant is closed, Yu and Jiang have supper together before the stove using whatever ingredients are left, wash the dishes, and call it a day. He knows what Jiang likes, so their supper is always something that he does. One day, as they were having noodles in the kitchen, Jiang suddenly asked Yu what he liked to eat. Yu takes in a mouthful of noodles and answers without giving it much thought:
'Everything. Can't be a cook if you don't like to eat, after all.'

lore.title: Archive File 4
lore.text:
Some time has passed since the first piece of selfhood fell.
Fragments fall off the source and find new life on this land.
It continues to dream in Its eternal slumber.
Ages pass, and the fury has gone to rest with sleep. The proxy born carrying Its most violent wish has devoted himself to the path of martial arts and cut off his connection with It.
It does not understand.
Why do the consciousnesses born of It now defy It?
Each fragment's identity has been shaped by their contact with mankind. They have become like mankind.
It does not understand.
They have joined forces to break free of Its influence, just as the mortals who received Its blessings did centuries ago.
It does not understand.
......
I do not understand. That is why I must seek, try, experiment. That is the first step to understanding.
Have I said this before? Turn one's eyes towards mankind, and what one sees is a ball of fire.
I cannot let fear stay my steps. Look. People gather around a fire, and place the prey they hunted above it.
Why do they do that? But I smell a pleasant aroma.
I shall understand.
I will begin with fire, which I am most curious about, and which I fear the most.
......
Pick up firewood and place it in a pile. I have lit my own fire. Put a skewer through the meat, and roast it on the fire. People come to me, drawn by the scent, and sit by my side. They have brought food with them. We share food with each other. It is of a different taste. The more I share, the more I sense the difference. And so, I became a chef—it is what they call those who make a living through cooking. I want to know all the tastes of that past, and what these tastes can bring others.
Cooking does not necessarily require a stove. A pot and a fire is all it takes. But people come back when there is a stove, and connections are built when people come back.
Where there is fire, there is smoke. Those who see the smoke and fire know that there is food here. Some eat here all their lives; others buy a snack once and never return. Even if everything outside is covered in ice and snow, they feel less cold once they sit down here and have something hot to eat. Perhaps they will remember the warmth of the fire and the flavor that filled their mouths, and come back to this place again.
I have seen people of all kinds and made cuisine of all kinds. The more I made, the less I understood, and the less I cared. I wanted an answer, but it was a question without one. Seek not perfection; joy lies the mundane journey of everyday life.
It seems I have no use for my powers. They should be returned to Me. Sleepy-head needs this 'vitality' more than I do. There are worse things than having this fire that never goes out light the room and warm my bed, but I cannot return my meaning so easily.
That little speck of doubt, that curiosity that created the future for mankind and sowed the seeds of suffering for myself, needs to be put back in the wok and fried again.

lore.title: Promotion Record
lore.text:
A beast glints jet as glaze, meal made—
The engraver put down his chisel after the first few words.
The inscriptions on the other eleven steles were written by him. He had lived a long life and seen the living myths, and should have had no difficulty writing the dedications.
But in Yu's case...
He wiped his chisel on his sleeves a few times, and finally decided to erase the words he had carved.
No one had seen Yu's Sui form.
But the first eleven used the same format. Surely the twelfth... no!
Form and order had been broken, like a candle in the middle of an incense burner, a most jarring sight.
He could imagine Yu's form, based on his hair, arms, and tail, but the rest...
The engraver fiddled with his beard, but could not come up with a good way to summarize Yu's deeds.
The rest of the family have the ability to move mountains and seas. He couldn't very well write 'It cooks real good' for this one!
Even the legend that Yu had cooked for the True Lung seemed far-fetched and unsophisticated compared to the deeds of the other eleven. But if one were to truly record Yu's deeds, one would also find them too numerous to be listed on one little stele.
He had been working on this for months already. The Sui Regulator was pressing him for updates every two or three days. If he cannot finish the stele by the end of the month... A penalty from the Sui Regulator is one thing. His fame, his reputation as a master poet, which he had spent a century building, would be ruined.
Sigh...
'How's the stele going, old man?' The young chef picked a most inopportune time to show up. 'So much easier than my siblings, isn't it?'
'Not in a million years!'

lore.title: Archive File 1
lore.text:
After she returned from Higashi, and before she took over the leadership of the L.G.D. Special Inspection Unit, Hoshiguma's first visit back to Rhodes Island was greeted with a mob of questions from other operators who had worked with her before:
'Did you change jobs, Hoshiguma/Operator Hoshiguma/Madame Oni?'
The misunderstanding was cleared up quickly. She came with Swire's permission, and was here to sign a cooperation agreement with Rhodes Island on a personal basis. The L.G.D. needed a channel of communications with Rhodes Island, and Hoshiguma was the best choice, given her new role at the SIU and what she had gone through with Rhodes Island together.
Her outfit, her sword, and the rather changed appearance of Hannya had little to do with her new role. According to her, she had simply gone back to Mitsukue to get some stuff while 'Missy' was on vacation in Siesta.
As for 'avoiding suspicion', the pair certainly had more to keep in mind, but the unusual respect and solemnness that Hoshiguma showed when she saw Swire could not be explained with just 'avoiding suspicion'.
We eventually found out the reason in a chance encounter between the pair—
'You just wanted to see me feeling awkward, didn't you?!'
'I-It's not what you think, Missy, at least not entirely—'
'Not entirely?'
'Well, mostly not—'
'That's a black mark on your record! No more vacations until you submit all the reports you have piled up!'

lore.title: Archive File 2
lore.text:
A subtle change seems to have come over Hoshiguma. She will do things that surprise others from time to time, such as openly making fun of Swire, clearly expressing her disapproval of Lungmen's less savory aspects, and on one occasion, placing her hand on the shoulder of someone who was abusing a medic. She said nothing, just smiled, and the troublemaker left the ward without argument.
The way she fights has changed as well. In addition to protecting more vulnerable comrades, she also charges into the fray, disintegrating enemy lines in a frenzied rampage. Some operators found Hoshiguma's new style to be terrifying at first, but they soon realize that she remains as protective as ever. She has never harmed a comrade in her rampages, and more importantly remained the same Madame Oni even when it seemed she had lost all reason: loyal, kind, a heavy drinker, as learned as she is strong.

[Classified Log]
There are many Higashinese accounts of how the Oni lose their reason in battle, cutting down anyone in their way, friend or foe. This perception is not unfounded. It is fundamentally the same as a Vampire's affinity for blood, or a Cyclops's ability to foresee misfortune. Without a Royal Court, however, these powers were never properly studied and refined, and the Oni had to explore how to live with their nature on their own. It is said that the temples may have engaged in such research, but their legacy is not witchcraft, but wisdom and a unique faith. Without the presence of a Royal Court, however, the Oni were able to integrate themselves into Higashinese society, making them unique amongst the Sarkaz of Terra.
Yes, the Oni are a branch of the Sarkaz. For the people of Higashi, this is something that might never occur to them their entire lives, but would feel entirely natural if someone pointed it out. Following customs, avoiding troubling others, blending in... this is the way of things in Higashi. Be it out of benevolence or some other reason, certain things are better left unsaid.
This ambiguity gives the Oni a kind of protection. In Accounts of Long Ago and a Digest of Records, they were known as 'man-oni', mentioned alongside the Ægirian 'sharkfolk'. Their stories of loyalty and mystique cannot be separated from Higashi without cutting off a big part of Higashinese tradition.
That said, just because they are not outsiders does not mean there are no complaints about them. The popular conception of the Oni is one of anger and violence, and there are many stereotypes about them: barbaric, cunning, uncouth, corrupt, etc. These are often contradictory, and rarely mentioned within earshot of an Oni. The intercity net is another matter though. Mentioning such things on the intercity net is likely to incite an angry response, but one could always say, 'Why are you so angry? Are you one of those rotten Oni too?'
—From the essay collection Gazes, written by a Victorian Sarkaz living in Higashi

lore.title: Archive File 3
lore.text:
[From a volunteer-maintained encyclopedia]
The First Kajimachi Conflict
The First Kajimachi Conflict refers to a violent conflict that occurred in Kajimachi in 1073. Stragglers who remained in Southern Court territory after the Bloodpeak Campaign attacked the Kinsekikai, attempting to take over Kajimachi. The Kinsekikai won a hard-fought victory, but the founding chairman of the Kinsekikai was killed in the struggle, along with the entire immediate family of Tessai, who was his chief lieutenant.
After fending off the attacks, Tessai, as the new chairman of the Kinsekikai, began hunting down those involved in the attacks, resulting in the largest and longest violent conflict in Mitsukue's history. Some see it as an act of revenge by Tessai for the killing of his family, while others see it as Tessai expanding his own influence.

The Second Kajimachi Conflict
The Second Kajimachi Conflict refers to a series of murders, violent conflicts, and disappearances that occurred around Kajimachi in 1078. The first phase involved the killing of legislator candidate Shinjirou Koretou by the Kinsekikai and its subsequent internal conflict; the second phase involved the intensification of the Kinsekikai exclusion movement that Shinjirou Koretou had spearheaded, resulting in several conflicts between the Kinsekikai and nearby residents; the third phase involved the Kinsekikai's admission that Hoshiguma, wakagashira at that time, had committed the murder and Hoshiguma's subsequent disappearance, with Kinbee Harada (later known as Kouhei Mifune), then-wakagashira-hosa to the Kinsekikai's second-in-command, bringing the events to a close by mediating between the Kinsekikai and nearby residents.
Some believe that the aftermath of the conflict continues to this day, with Hoshiguma continuing to commit numerous murders in the shadows, but such claims lack evidence and conflict with police records and other verified sources. See also 'Kaidan of Mitsukue-taisha'

The Third Kajimachi Conflict (cached)
The Third Kajimachi Conflict refers to a series of attempted kidnappings, violent conflicts, murders, media manipulation, and assaults that occurred around Kajimachi and Nita Street in 1099. It began with the sudden reappearance of Hoshiguma, the former second-in-command of the Kinsekikai who had gone missing after being suspected of murder, after the statute of limitations had passed. Her return triggered a violent struggle between Kouhei Mifune, the Kinsekikai's de facto leader, and Tessai, the nominal chairman of the Kinsekikai whose authority had long been undermined. The entertainer Momoka Hanyuu was also known to be involved in the incident. Tessai was killed in the struggle, while Mifune was arrested. Hoshiguma voluntarily departed Mitsukue after reaching an agreement with Mitsukue police, and Momoka Hanyuu departed the Kinseki Talent Agency to continue her activities independently. The incident also dispelled the myths around most of the Kaidan of Mitsukue-taisha.

Murder of the Kinsekikai Chairman (Active Page)
(Redirected from 'The Third Kajimachi Conflict'
The murder of the Kinsekikai chairman occurred in Kajimachi in 1099, when Kouhei Mifune murdered Tessai, chairman of the Kinsekikai. Mifune, who had been in conflict with Tessai over the Kinsekikai's succession and future, humiliated Tessai, forced a crippling debt upon him, and murdered him at his own residence. Mifune was subsequently arrested by the police.

lore.title: Archive File 4
lore.text:
[Tessai's Diary]
Visited Haruuji Arimagawa for the fifth time and concluded the transaction. I finally gained the secret scroll that his ancestor had obtained from the temple's via less-than-scrupulous means. The paper is yellow and brittle, but the ink has not faded, and I was able to recognize part of the cursive script used. It appears authentic. More importantly, the Arimagawa clan is no longer the noble house that once claimed the position of high minister. Haruuji is merely an ordinary man, making ends meet by selling off family possessions. He would not dare deceive me.
It will not be long before I can no longer wield a hammer at the forge. I must personally oversee the production of crystalline components; it is not a task I can entrust to anyone else. Hoshiguma is not suited for it; Shimasu and Sanoguchi say they want to learn, but they are merely going through the motions. Kinbee has put in the work, but he has a long way to go. He will be a competent assistant for Hoshiguma when she takes over the position of chairman.
......
Kinbee told me that Hoshiguma and Shimasu almost got into a fight. Fortunately, Hoshiguma was able to hold back; a feud between clan-siblings would have to be dealt with according to the rules, and even Hoshiguma would be no exception. Regarding Hoshiguma, her father [scrawled out]
The matter of the shield cannot wait. I have had a monk translate the scroll. Other than the scripture at the beginning, neither a preface nor a summary, the rest is undoubtedly instructions for weapon-crafting.
......
'Hannya.'
This word, found in the beginning of the opening scripture, has occupied my mind of late as I worked at the forge. The monk told me that 'Hannya' was a wisdom that transcended the mortal realm and liberated one from all troubles. But he does not know why the word became the name of the terrifying 'Face of Hannya'.
But it is that same face that always comes back to me whenever I swing my hammer. The rage as he drew his sword against Tetsuya, against Hoshiguma, against me. The fear as he fell to the ground. The despair in those last moments of lucidity, as he realized what he had done.
I told Hoshiguma many times that the dastardly deserter was the only one to blame. It was not her father's fault, and certainly not her fault. She understood. She knew I did not blame her. And she knew that I could not help but hate Susa.
He killed Tetsuya. He had held Tetsuya in his arms and gave him his old stethoscope as a toy. He had given Tetsuya his injection when Tetsuya had a fever, and bought him the latest trending drink in town, which not even Hoshiguma had tried. Apart from Setsuko and myself, he was the dearest person to Tetsuya, dearer than even Tetsuya's own grandmother. If I did the same and pulled my sword against Hoshiguma—
......
Is there no liberation for the Oni, other than death?
I was never freed. I exacted vengeance upon all the Oni who dared set foot in Kajimachi that night. I watched them cry helplessly, watched them go mad, watched them die, but I was never free.
I told myself that I was forging this shield for Hoshiguma, so that she would never repeat your mistake. But perhaps... it was always my own liberation that I was seeking.
Were you free at the end of it all, Susa?

lore.title: Promotion Record
lore.text:
My surname?
I asked Uncle Tessai after my father's death. People called him Tessai, called my father Susa, and called me Hoshiguma. None of us had surnames. Other people did; Aunt Setsuko's surname was Inaba, but she no longer had one after she married Uncle Tessai.
It's not a particularly interesting story. Are you sure you want to hear it?
Well, I guess I can tell you over a drink.
The widely-accepted explanation is that the practice of the Oni using only a given name began after Seisaku Onishoubu's death. Many of his descendants joined the temples and discarded their real names in favor of dharma names, in order to avoid trouble. On the other hand, there are also people who falsely claim to be descendants of Onishoubu, including some who truly worship him.
The problem is that you could walk into a room with a bunch of Oni, call out the name Saburo, and have three or four of them turn around to look at you. Which created problems for everything from taxation to battlefield command. That's why the Northern Court issued the 'Obligation of Surnames for All People'; the Southern Court had similar laws, essentially demanding that the Oni respect the tradition of the 'surname bestowed by the Sumeragimi', and restore their original surnames. The problem is that too much time had passed, and it was unclear who was trying to avoid trouble, and who was trying to benefit by association. Besides, both sides prohibited Oni without surnames from claiming the name of Onishoubu, and many people simply didn't cooperate. The whole thing basically went away quietly.
Uncle Tessai said both my family and his were branches of the Onishoubu clan; mine specialized in medicine and divination, while his specialized in weapons and armor. If we were to restore our surnames, we would call ourselves 'Jigokuin' or 'Toujiin'... I don't quite remember. I wouldn't take everything Uncle Tessai said at face value either. That bit about medicine and divination and weapons and armor might just have been him projecting us onto our ancestors.
What? ...Hah, no. Just like how Missy gets angry when I call her 'commissioner', I'd rather you didn't add some weird surname to 'Hoshiguma'. Names like 'Susa' and 'Hoshiguma' don't really fit well with a surname anyway.
Last time I came to Rhodes Island, there was a Sarkaz historian who thought I might be related to the famous Qui'lon after he saw my blue flames... Personally, I don't believe it. I do believe that his migration to the east brought the Anasa and Oni to Yan and Higashi, but I don't see the point in further speculation. It's not like Missy would increase my pay if I was Qui'lon's descendant.
...What do you mean 'I didn't expect you to actually be as well-read as Wei Yenwu said'? We see each other for the first time in ages, and all you can do is tease me? It's getting late, and the training room's free. How about you fulfill my wish, and Uncle Tessai's?
Tsk, you still can't hold your drink.
Alright, stop trying to act tough, Ch'en. I'll take you back to your room.

lore.title: Archive File 1
lore.text:
[Industry Commentary: Braving the Forbidden—Reform or Rehash?]
There seems to be little point in talking about 'forbidden' areas in a land that is 90% uninhabited.
On this land tilled by Catastrophe for thousands of years, even wilderness level enough for nomadic cities to traverse is rare, much less fertile soil suited for farming. For city-dwellers who think fowlbeast meat is grown in supermarkets directly in their packages, ready to be cooked, the nomadic cities and the wilderness visible from their routes are the entirety of Terra. They do not think of other places as 'distant' or 'dangerous', because they do not think of those places at all.
As such, 'travel' in the traditional sense is more like a vacation. Caravan International Travel Agency can take you to Sami, but all you will see is a well-furnished Sami-style resort village. It will feel no different from a Columbian nomadic city, at least once you spend a few days acclimating to the cold.
In recent years, however, Columbian tourism has become fascinated with the forbidden. News reports of the wealthy hiring guides to take them into forbidden areas are a regular occurrence, and travel agencies have started marketing these 'forbidden tours'. Naturally, the authorities responded by stepping up their control of such areas. Last year, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Arts Units, and Originium, the Columbian Park Police, and the army's Mobile Cavalry came to an accord regarding management division of the Bleached Wasteland, drafting a patrol route that fully covers the region.
As for the reason...

'It's true that enforcement has gotten stricter, but that has nothing to do with those so-called 'forbidden tours'. Two tour guides dressed up in military uniforms pretend to check your papers, then you take a few photos in a place that looks empty enough—that's all that 'forbidden tour' crap is about.
'If you want to see caverns with naturally occurring liquefied Originium, or Feranmut carcasses lying in the desert—the stuff you'd have to risk your hide to see...
'Then look for Ferne Barn.
'Me? Forget it, I'm not taking anyone with me, no way.
'Ferne's the only one with the skills AND the willingness to bring people along. You wanna go, find her.'
—Operator Asbestos, when asked about 'forbidden tours'

lore.title: Archive File 2
lore.text:
Ferne Barn, citizen of Columbia.
Investigation reveals that she has registered more than twenty accounts with seven banks in fifteen different Columbian nomadic cities, using different identities.
After tracking the cashflow of these accounts, we found Ferne's spending patterns to be extremely suspicious. Virtually all expenses are for medical bills, medicine, luxury items, antiques, as well as fines and bails paid to law enforcement authorities. There are no signs of spending on any ordinary items, be it food, clothing, housing, or any basic daily necessities.
Therefore, we believe that this 'Ferne Barn' does not actually exist: she is simply a persona created by criminal organizations to facilitate their illicit activities...
—Internal Revenue Department Investigative Report

When I first saw the operator who was to serve as my guide on the mission, she was crawling on top of her dorm room's closet. She tossed me a package before I asked.
'Here! Your onboarding equipment!' She said.
It was a bunch of junk. Broken telephone wires, tattered tarp pieces, safety ropes that had lost their buckles—and looked like they might have already taken a few lives—and plastic ties that looked straight out of a scrap heap.
'What's the matter? I gave you the best stuff!' She looked downright proud.
I pointed at the tattered tarp, then at myself, and shot her a doubtful look.
'...Ah! I forgot to give you scissors! One moment.'
Suddenly, I understood. She was wearing the same equipment she gave me: a telephone wire as a hair tie, a piece of tarp as her skirt, a safety rope as her belt, and used plastic ties to fasten her protective gear and communicator. This junk was her agency's 'equipment'.
As I took out my wallet, I saw her smile disappear.
'Please put that away. This agency does not require its employees to foot the bill.'
But she didn't even have the money for proper equipment!
'It's called smart spending! You gotta build connections with doctors and medicine dealers in case a customer gets sick or gets hurt, and you wanna be in the good graces of the ATAO, Rangers, and Mobile Cavalry officials so they don't arrest or 'accidentally' shoot your clients! That's where the money goes. As for equipment... what's the problem? Is the hair tie inconvenient? Is the belt not solid enough?'
—Rhodes Island Field Operator Report

lore.title: Archive File 3
lore.text:
After a long and drawn-out process, the Trimounts City Administration finally announced that they were closing the investigation into the recent incidents.
With reluctance written all over his face, a city spokesman admitted that the 'savage' (who was smashing walnuts with a briefcase as the spokesman emphasized the word), two meters tall and with indecipherable symbols painted all over his face with solidified Originium crystal, and who answered any questions with manglerbeast-like growling, was indeed a senior accountant of United Donuts Group whose papers were all in order.
The Administration had to admit another failure in just two weeks: they failed in stopping this 'senior accountant' from riding into the wilderness atop of a box truck containing one thousand two hundred hard-shelled briefcases. Fifty kilometers north of the end of the Trimounts route, in a forest that exists in a strange state of symbiosis with active Originium, the lives of one thousand two hundred natives unknown to Columbia were about to change dramatically. With these one thousand two hundred hard-shelled briefcases, they would be able to easily crack open the mutated Originium slugs indigenous to the area, which were their main source of nutrition. The one who brought such a wonderful tool back to the tribe would become a hero. He would be able to have the first pick of the freshest Originium slugs, and his tribe would build a statue of him with solidified Originium crystal.
The man himself, however, seemed to have different ideas.
Soon, the two meter-tall 'senior accountant' was once again spotted on the streets of Trimounts. Quickly encircled by a swarm of excited reporters and the sulking city spokesman who kept cursing at the sight of this grand comeback, the man took out, with a proud look on his face, two calculators and began to play an unfathomable beat on the buttons. Apparently, he enjoyed creating chaos in this unfamiliar city far more than accepting his tribesmen's tribute of Originium slugflesh.
City Administration officials submitted multiple requests to authorize a warrant, but all of those reports to their normally swift and decisive superior went unanswered. After one week, they finally lost patience and kicked down the door to their boss's office, only to find it empty. Seventy kilometers east of the end of the Trimouts route, in a Durin-occupied ruin deep under a metal megastructure, their boss was muttering drunkenly with a cup of strong mushroom wine in his hand.

Few know that a guide by the name of Ferne Barn was behind all this, from the flawless paperwork of the 'senior accountant', to the silent disappearance of a City Administration official. For her part, Ferne seemed uninterested in this farce of her own making. Was it a prank, a social experiment, a marketing ploy, or a show? Ferne never said a thing, even when speculation was at its peak.
The reporters might be fascinated by the presence of a savage on the streets of the city of progress, and the officials might be devastated that their superior had been reduced to a drunkard living in ruins with the Durin, but Ferne simply found it utterly natural that anyone might want to be anywhere and lead any kind of life.

'Is it strange for me to think that way? ...I guess it might be. But the job of a guide is to fulfill those dreams, isn't it?'

lore.title: Archive File 4
lore.text:
Our living room was always filled with children listening to Dad's stories when I came back from school.
None of the children came to Dad's funeral, but there was an uninvited guest who interrupted the ritual with blaring sirens. A potbellied cop poked his head out of the patrol car, saying he had received complaints from parents about someone by the name of Martin Barn, who deceived children with tales of gold-scaled sandbeasts and the like—
The cop stopped mid-sentence, took a look at us, then at the name on the coffin, and left without another word.
Sheriff Jones of Trenton—I nailed the name to the wall when I founded the travel agency, hoping to prove to him one day that Dad wasn't a scammer, and gold-scaled sandbeasts were real.
In the last few years, I proved a lot of things to a lot of people. Some didn't believe there were nomadic cities outside of Columbia, some believed the Pioneers' treasure was hidden in the Bleached Wasteland... I let them see the truth with their own eyes, but was never able to prove the existence of gold-scaled sandbeasts.
I had theories. The steppe-dwelling sandbeasts usually have multiple layers of backfins in order to blend into their surroundings, which could easily be mistaken for scales at a distance. Maybe sandbeasts that dwell in golden steppes rich in Originium really do look like they have golden scales. Another theory was that the people of Rim Billiton had tamed small sandbeasts for use in the mines—the capillaries in their backfins can help with determining air conditions in the tunnels, and people sometimes would paste golden foil on their backfins for easier identification. Was that what Dad saw?
It makes sense, doesn't it? But there's no proof. It helps people understand how these stories could come about, but it doesn't stop them from thinking Dad was lying.
Besides, Sheriff Jones passed away two years ago.
—Ferne Barn, on a rare occasion when she spoke about her father

Sandbeasts are small, fluffy animals, while gold-scaled sandbeasts exist only as drawings in picture books, or as curiosities in tabloid columns. And for many years, Martin Barn was the sole supplier of such columns for the Columbian tabloid industry.
Columbian archives consider such tabloids to be beneath them, and Ferne never saw those columns again after Martin passed away. That is, until she came to Rhodes Island.
The column on the page was accompanied by a shoddy illustration of a gold-scaled sandbeast, which looked like someone had copied and pasted the texture of a pineapple. The newspaper had become creased with age, but someone had carefully flattened the creases before pasting the cutting in a notebook. The Cautus with bangs like a pinwheel cookie gazed intently into Ferne's eyes.
'You want me to help you find this creature?'
The Cautus nodded fervently.
'You believe it exists?'
The Cautus cocked her head in confusion. She said she did not know whether she believed in it or not. It wasn't a question she had even thought about.
She had simply heard a story and wanted to see it for herself.
The Cautus asked if whether she believed in it or not was important. Should she?
'No, it's not important. Let's go find it!'

lore.title: Promotion Record
lore.text:
Rusthammer 'Fiends Gang' camp, forty-three kilometers east of Lake Sulligan. Two people were tied up and hung upside-down from an arch made of bones.
'Are you REALLY sure about this, Ferne? This ain't a movie where the cavalry come riding to the rescue in the nick of time! You saw that blind devil yourself! He could break my neck with his fingers! Are you SURE you made the arrangements? Are you REALLY sure those people are coming? Say something already! We're gonna die!'
'Hm... I never realized that this is how the land looks upside-down.'
'?'
'Say, don't those houses look like boats when they're upside down?'
'We've only got a few more minutes left to live, and this is what you wanna talk about?'
'It's precisely because we've only got a few more minutes that I wanna take a good long look.'
Two minutes later, an armored ambulance with the words 'Mandrake International Wilderness Rescue' charged through the west-side fence, and the crew pointed three ballistae at the executioner who was polishing his blade. Meanwhile, on the east side of the camp, a man wearing a metal bucket on his head leisurely got off his burdenbeast and waved at the crew of the ambulance, gesturing that there was still room for negotiation.
'You know, upside-down trees look kinda like toilet brushes.'
